correctness.rationale: A facet of a (2r−1)-sphere contains exactly 2r vertices, so each r-tuple simplex has dimension <=1. For the initial boundary of a 2r-simplex the tuple graph is KG(2r+1,r), connected through Johnson one-swap moves and shared disjoint neighbor, with V=binom(2r+1,r), E=(r+1)/2·V. Stacking F deletes exactly binom(2r,r)/2 old complementary-pair edges, adds binom(2r,r−1) new vertices and r·binom(2r,r) new edges. The replacement bipartite graph is connected: neighboring old r-subsets of F share the new vertex indexed by their r−1 element complement; the old Johnson graph is connected. Therefore no deleted edge disconnects a component and the new vertices attach. Euler rank increment (r−1)/2·binom(2r+1,r) proves the formula integrally without finite extrapolation. Independently rebuilt all tuple graph edges for r=3 through two stackings (V35,E70, beta36; V50,E120,beta71; V65,E170,beta106) and r=4 through one stacking (V126,E315,beta190 to V182,E560,beta379).
residual_risks: Independent enumerations cover only r=3,4 examples; arbitrary r and stacking depth follow the explicit local proof.
